desc:
The array nums may contain repeated values. Two subsets are considered the same when they contain every value the same number of times, no matter which positions the values were taken from. For example, in [1, 2, 2] the two subsets that pick a single 2 are the same subset.

Return the number of distinct subsets, counting the empty subset, modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: Listing all the distinct subsets only works for tiny arrays. Count them instead of generating them.
A distinct subset is described completely by how many copies of each distinct value it takes. Those choices are independent.
A value that occurs c times can be taken 0, 1, ..., c times, which is c + 1 options. Multiply these option counts over all distinct values.
editorial: Group equal values together. A subset (in the sense of this problem) is fixed by choosing, for every distinct value, how many copies to use. A value with c occurrences offers c + 1 choices, and the choices for different values do not influence each other, so the total is the product of (c + 1) over all distinct values. The empty subset corresponds to choosing zero copies everywhere and is counted automatically.

Check with [1, 2, 2]: the value 1 gives 2 options and the value 2 gives 3 options, so 6 distinct subsets: [], [1], [2], [1,2], [2,2], [1,2,2]. Building them with backtracking would take exponential time; counting needs one pass with a hash map. Take the product modulo 109+7 at every step.
